Arise Infra Pty Ltd, located in Reedy Creek, QLD, is seeking a skilled and motivated Civil Engineering Technician to join its growing team on a full-time basis. Arise Infra Pty Ltd is a Queensland-based business operating in the residential design and construction space, with a strong focus on tailored home design solutions and a client-centred approach to project delivery. The business is built around customised design outcomes, practical planning and close collaboration with clients throughout the design and building process, and presents itself as a Queensland home-building and custom design studio that delivers bespoke homes and supports clients across every stage of their project. This role will suit a candidate who can support civil and site works, carry out technical assessments and testing, and contribute to the accurate and compliant delivery of the infrastructure that underpins the company’s residential projects.

Position: Civil Engineering Technician

Location: Reedy Creek, QLD

Key Responsibilities
•	Interpreting project briefs, engineering instructions and work assignments to determine suitable methods, procedures and equipment for each civil and site-related task across the company’s residential and associated development projects
•	Preparing sketches, plans, layouts, schedules, charts and tabulations for civil works such as site drainage, stormwater management, water and sewer service connections, internal access roads, driveways, pavements and other supporting infrastructure
•	Collecting, reviewing and analysing site and project data and carrying out calculations relating to levels, grades, quantities, drainage capacities and material requirements
•	Carrying out and directing on-site fieldwork and related testing to support design, set-out and construction activities across active project sites
•	Conducting and arranging field and laboratory testing of soils, fill and construction materials to confirm their suitability for foundations, pavements and earthworks, and gathering site, access and survey data to inform servicing and traffic arrangements for developments
•	Estimating material quantities and costs for civil and site works and helping ensure that completed works meet project specifications, relevant standards, approval conditions and contract provisions
•	Inspecting civil and site works during and after construction and organising and supervising any required rectification, maintenance or repair to maintain quality and compliance
•	Preparing the supporting civil documentation, drawings and technical data required for council and authority submissions, approvals and construction certification
•	Checking dimensions, levels, set-out and site details against approved plans to support accuracy and buildability on site
•	Liaising with designers, engineers, surveyors, contractors, site supervisors and external consultants to coordinate civil and construction information across each project
•	Maintaining organised records of site data, test results, calculations, drawings and revisions for project control and future reference
•	Monitoring works on site to confirm they are completed in line with relevant building, drainage and construction standards and practical site conditions
•	Contributing to continuous improvement in technical processes, documentation quality and efficiency across the company’s projects

Skills and Experience
•	at least 1 year of relevant work experience
•	an AQF associate degree, advanced diploma or diploma in a relevant field

Personal Attributes
•	strong attention to detail and a commitment to accurate, high-quality technical work
•	able to manage competing deadlines and adapt to changing project priorities
•	a clear communicator with a collaborative, team-focused approach
•	practical, methodical and solution-focused in approach
•	reliable and capable of working both independently and as part of a project team, on site and in the office

Employment Type: Full-time | Hours: 38 hours per week

Salary: $75,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation per annum

If you are a capable Civil Engineering Technician looking for a full-time opportunity in Reedy Creek, QLD, we encourage you to apply.

result.description:
A Building Associate supervises construction sites and organises and coordinates the material and human resources required for a project.

Role Overview
Phoeniks is seeking an experienced Building Associate to supervise and coordinate the construction-related aspects of its ventilated ceiling installation projects nationally. The role sits within Phoeniks' technical and construction supervision function, assisting Construction Managers, Architects and Engineers in the planning, feasibility assessment, and on-site delivery of ventilated ceiling works across commercial, healthcare and institutional projects.

The successful candidate will act as Phoeniks' supervising construction sites, coordinating labour and materials, interpreting plans and codes, and ensuring works are feasible, compliant, and delivered to specification.

Key Responsibilities
1. Assisting Construction Managers, Architects and Surveyors in Planning and Organisation
- Support Construction Managers, Architects and Engineers in planning and organising ventilated ceiling works, including sequencing, access and integration with the broader head-contractor construction program
- Provide technical input during project planning, value engineering and problem-solving stages, working closely with the Product Manager and Technical Manager

2. Interpreting Plans, Regulations and Codes of Practice
- Read and interpret architectural and engineering drawings, specifications and construction documentation for ventilated ceiling installations
- Interpret and apply Australian Standards, building codes, and WHS regulations relevant to ceiling and building services works

3. Preparing Preliminary Sketches, Working Drawings and Specifications
- Prepare preliminary installation sketches and site-specific working drawings for ventilated ceiling systems
- Develop method statements and installation specifications tailored to individual site conditions

4. Preparing, Editing and Revising Plans, Maps, Charts and Drawings
- Edit and revise installation drawings, ceiling layout plans and services coordination charts in response to site conditions, clashes or design changes
- Liaise with the Product Manager – Ventilated Ceilings on drawing updates arising from product-specific requirements or site variations

5. Coordinating Works Programs
- Coordinate ventilated ceiling installation programs and sequencing across multiple sites nationally, aligning with the head contractor's overall construction program
- Supervise and support installation teams and subcontractors to ensure correct methods, sequencing and workmanship
- Assist with commissioning and handover activities as required

6. Inspecting Work and Materials for Compliance with Specifications, Regulations and Standards
- Attend project sites to inspect in-progress and completed works, ceiling structures, and materials for compliance with drawings, specifications and Australian Standards
- Conduct quality checks, identify defects, risks or required rework, and provide clear technical feedback to internal teams
- Ensure all site activities comply with WHS regulations, site safety plans and Phoeniks procedures

7. Calculating Costs and Estimating Time Scales
- Estimate installation time scales, labour requirements and material costs for ventilated ceiling projects, feeding into project programs and budgets
- Assess the technical feasibility of proposed installations prior to project confirmation, identifying risks, constraints and cost implications for internal teams

8. Collecting Data Using Surveying Instruments and Photogrammetric Equipment
- Collect on-site measurement and survey data — levels, dimensions, structural grid and services coordination data — using appropriate surveying and measuring instruments
- Record site conditions using photographic and measurement-based survey methods to support pre- installation feasibility assessments

9. Performing Routine Computations and Plotting Preliminary Data
- Perform routine dimensional, load and quantity computations to support installation drawings and material take-offs
- Plot preliminary layout and survey data to inform installation planning and drawing preparation

Training & Knowledge Transfer
- Train Phoeniks installation teams and subcontractors nationally on ventilated ceiling systems, promoting best-practice installation methods and quality standards across all regions
- Develop and deliver practical, on-site and workshop-based training sessions

Skills & Experience
Essential
- Relevant qualification or at least three years of relevant industry experience
- Proven experience supervising construction sites, ceiling systems, HVAC-related installations, or building services installations
- Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, specifications and construction documentation
- Strong understanding of site conditions, services coordination and construction sequencing
- Ability to collect and interpret site survey/measurement data and perform routine technical computations
- Willingness and ability to travel nationally on a regular basis
- Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with Construction Managers, Architects, Engineers and internal teams

Desirable
- Experience with ventilated ceilings, chilled beams, or integrated ceiling systems
- Trade or associate-level qualification in construction, mechanical services, or a related field
- Experience working on healthcare, commercial, or large-scale construction projects
- Familiarity with Australian Standards and building codes relevant to ceilings and services
- Registration or licensing relevant to building supervision (where applicable)

result.description:
Leica Geosystems Pty Ltd, trading as Hexagon is a technology company. Our mission is to put data to work autonomously – to measure progress and improve outcomes. We partner with mining companies uniting each individual and their data for informed decision making. We do this by connecting systems to work autonomously with data from all other systems - so those systems are no longer working in isolation. For mining companies to remain competitive, they must be efficient and proactive; connect processes and people for faster decision-making. With our world class sensors, software and technology that make sense of data in real time – mines can be safer, more sustainable, and make smarter decisions.  
We are seeking a Senior Autonomous Application Engineer to join our Autonomous Road Train Engineering team. In this role, you will lead ongoing support for the integration and deployment of autonomous systems within our technology, operational, and production environments. You will ensure quality, testing, and validation requirements are aligned between field teams and product development, while working directly with customers to provide technical consultation and deliver solutions that meet quality targets.
This role serves as the in-country representative of a global engineering team, acting as the critical link between local field teams and global product development teams.
Operating independently, the position requires ability to work across a diverse stakeholder group, displaying ownership, initiative, and the ability to navigate on ground requirements in alignment with key engineering milestones. 
As a Senior Autonomous Application Engineer, you will play a critical role in interfacing between field teams, product development teams and customers to identify critical priorities and solutions in addition you will the responsible for, but not limited to;
•	Providing front line product and application support and leadership to address product quality and functional insufficiency issues for both internal and external customers
•	Serve as Subject Matter Expert on autonomous technologies, system architecture, troubleshooting, and performance optimization.
•	Developing and optimizing software running on embedded systems and linux based platforms
•	Serve as the Subject Matter Expert on telematics-based messaging and machine protocols such as network and CAN
•	Build and integrate applications that support perception, planning, localization, navigation, and machine control.
•	Manage complex technical issues, perform root-cause analysis, and coordinate resolutions to ensure high customer satisfaction and system reliability
•	Working directly with customers to understand requirements, provide technical consultations and deliver tailored solutions that meet quality targets
•	Performing software testing, verification, bug reports, and field trial coordination
Technical
•	Degree in Geomatics, Electrical Engineering or related field
•	10+ years of relevant experience 
•	Prior experience in autonomous technology ideally from concept through to testing/validation and commissioning
•	Understanding and exposure to Autonomous technology in automotive or ASH/Mining environments
•	Understanding of auto electrical application in heavy industrial environments or mining
•	Proven problem solving/ troubleshooting skills
•	Exceptional interpersonal skills and ability to get on with others
•	English fluency with excellent verbal and written skills
•	Ability to work across global time zones
